F.  PUBLIC HEARINGS:

  AGENDA
  ITEM 5:  PLANNED DEVELOPMENT PERMIT PD-22-17
   2708 Birch Street
   Request: This is an application to demolish an existing 1,127 square
  foot single-family dwelling and detached one-car garage and develop
  a new 1,332 square foot, two-story single-family dwelling with an
  attached two-car garage at the front of the property, hereby referred
  to as Building A, and a new 1,552 square foot, two-story single-family
  dwelling with an attached two-car garage at the rear of the property,
  hereby referred to as Building B, on a site of approximately 8,250
  square feet located in the R-2 (Limited Multiple Family Residential)
  zone.
   Recommended Action: Adopt Resolution 22-35 approving Planned
  Development Permit PD-22-17, subject to the Conditions of
  Approval.
   Assistant Planner Kassandra Cornejo provided the Staff
  presentation.
   Johnny Yu, the applicant, was available to answer questions.
   Commissioner Comments:
   The Commissioners inquired if there were renderings of what the
  proposed new structures would look like.
   The Commissioners inquired if the proposed units would be for rental
  or for-sale, and whether the proposed project would be subject to the
  City’s Inclusionary Housing Ordinance.
   Public Comments:
  Johnny Yu indicated the property is currently owner occupied and
  the proposed new units will continue to be owner occupied, with only
  the proposed ADU potentially being rented out.
  Jennifer Ng commented that the use of shutters is inconsistent.

  3
  11/21/2022
 MOTION:

ITEM 6:  PLANNED DEVELOPMENT PERMIT PD-22-22, VARIANCE VAR-
  22-05, CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT CUP-22-09, AND FINDING OF
  PUBLIC CONVENIENCE OR NECESSITY
   214 West Main Street
   Request: This is an application for a Commercial Planned
  Development Permit, Variance, Conditional Use Permit, and Finding
  of Public Convenience or Necessity to establish a market with a Type
  20 (Off-Sale Beer and Wine) License in an existing commercial lease
  space with less than the number of required parking spaces located at
  214 West Main Street in the Central Business District (CBD) and
  Downtown Revitalization District zone.
   Recommended Action: Adopt Resolution 22-36 approving Planned
  Development Permit PD-22-22, Variance VAR-22-05, Conditional
  Use Permit CUP-22-09, and a Finding of Public Convenience or
  Necessity, subject to the Conditions of Approval.
   Assistant Planner Kassandra Cornejo provided the Staff
  presentation.
   Jay Zhao and Steven Chen, business owner and applicant,
  respectively, were available to answer questions.
   Commissioner Comments:
   The Commissioners thanked Assistant Planner Kassandra Cornejo for
  the thoroughness and clarity of the Staff report and presentation, and
  commended her work.
   The Commissioners inquired if the alcoholic beverage license will
  allow for the delivery of alcohol with groceries.
   Public Comments:
  Jay Zhao and Steven Chen clarified that the business will not deliver
  alcohol, and that most deliveries will consist of snacks and drinks.

MOTION:
    Moved to approve.
    Moved by Commissioner Olson, Seconded by Commissioner Pham.
    The motion carried by the following roll call vote:

  Ayes:  Juarez, Mojarro, Olson, Pham, Tsujii, Wang, Garcia, Gardea

G.  DISCUSSION ITEMS:

  AGENDA
  ITEM 3:  PRESENTATION ON EXISTING DOWNTOWN PARKING
  CONDITIONS AND PARKING DATA
   This is a presentation on existing parking conditions and parking data
  within the vicinity of the Downtown presented by Planning Division
  Staff.
   Recommended Action: It is recommended that the Planning
  Commission receive and file this informational report and provide
  input to Staff as deemed appropriate.
   Principal Planner Paul Lam provided the Staff presentation.
   Commissioner Comments:
   The Commissioners inquired if the estimated amount of street parking
  accounted for residential uses around the CBD and how much of
  estimated amount of street parking is being utilized by nearby
  residents.
   The Commissioners inquired if Staff had an estimate of the number
  of parking spaces available when taking into consideration that not all
  businesses are open at the same time.
   The Commissioners inquired if Staff has an estimate of when the
  highest demand for parking occurs.
   The Commissioners asked for clarification on whether the estimated
  Downtown parking demand is based upon the current Zoning Code
  requirements for parking, and whether the estimate considered
  existing vacant commercial tenant spaces. The Commissioners
  further inquired what the estimate might be if Staff were to assume
  full occupancy of all commercial tenant spaces, and asked Staff to
  look into this.
   The Commissioners inquired if Staff considered the number of
  overnight parking permits issued for the area in order to determine

  5
  11/21/2022
   how many residents utilize the street parking relative to patrons of
  downtown businesses.
    The Commissioners requested clarification on what is considered a
  permit space in the public parking facilities and whether there is a fee
  charged for the permit spaces.
    The Commissioners inquired as to how the new development to be
  constructed at the existing surface parking lot at 103 North Chapel
  Avenue will impact the total available parking.
    The Commissioners asked for additional clarification on the number
  of parking spaces in the two existing surface parking lots that will be
  redeveloped with affordable housing, and how the parking spaces that
  are being removed as a result of these projects will be recouped.
    The Commissioners inquired if the existing public parking structures
  were constructed under redevelopment or if there is a Business
  Improvement District that pays for these public parking facilities. The
  Commissioners indicated the City should consider how these public
  parking facilities are managed as a resource. The Commissioners
  further stated that the permits for the public parking facilities appear
  to give an advantage to certain businesses and there should be some
  sort of limit to ensure the facilities are not being dedicated entirely to
  employee parking.
    The Commissioners inquired into how many new residential units are
  proposed for the developments at 103 North Chapel Avenue and 11
  South First Street. The Commissioners also asked if parking is being
  provided for all of the new residential units.
    The Commissioners expressed concern with the potential for parking
  issues in the Downtown given that the parking demand already
  exceeds the parking capacity, and this estimated demand did not
  account for existing commercial vacancies. The Commissioners
  stated there is a need for management of parking facilities and
  allocation of permits.
    Public Comments:
  There were none.

MOTION:
    Moved to receive and file the informational report.
    Moved by Vice President Garcia, Seconded by Commissioner Olson.
    The motion carried by the following roll call vote:
  Roll Call Vote: 8-0
  Ayes:  Juarez, Mojarro, Olson, Pham, Tsujii, Wang, Garcia, Gardea
  Noes:  None
  Abstain: None
  Absent: Ho, Sahu

AGENDA
ITEM 4:  ZONING CODE UPDATE
   This is the sixth presentation in a series of presentations on the
  6
  11/21/2022
   Comprehensive Zoning Code Update project presented by Planning
  Division Staff.
  Recommended Action: It is recommended that the Planning
  Commission receive and file this informational report and provide
  input to Staff as deemed appropriate.
  Principal Planner Paul Lam provided the Staff presentation.
  Commissioner Comments – Off-Street Parking Standards
  Applicability:
  o The Commissioners inquired if references to additional units
  means additional leasable square footage or creation of new tenant
  spaces within existing square footage.
  o The Commissioners inquired where the 30% threshold was
  derived from. The Commissioners expressed concern with how
  scalable this threshold would be depending on various contexts.
  o The Commissioners asked if the City utilizes varying parking
  standards in different districts and specific plans, or if the same
  parking standards are used throughout the City. The
  Commissioners also asked if the proposed new parking
  requirements would replace any parking requirements identified
  in Specific Plans.
  o The Commissioners expressed that the proposed changes may
  create higher demand for street parking and asked Staff if there
  had been any study on this.
  o The Commissioners inquired if there is any additional rationale
  behind the proposed 30% threshold.
  o The Commissioners also asked for clarification if the proposed
  parking requirements in the new Zoning Code will apply to
  residential additions of 50% or more. The Commissioners
  followed up with additional questions on the current parking
  requirements for residential uses and whether the proposed
  changes would allow single-family residential uses to construct
  additions without having to provide additional parking to conform
  with the requirements.
  o The Commissioners suggested making the 30% threshold scalable
  as opposed to a uniform number applicable across the board.
  o The Commissioners asked Staff for confirmation that the area
  within a ½ mile radius of major transit stops includes roughly half
  of the Central Business District. The Commissioners further
  stated that there may be a need to tailor parking based on different
  districts.
  o The Commissioners requested Staff provide the Commission with
  a copy of the map of major transit stops and the ½ mile radius
  surrounding the major transit stops within the City.
  o The Commissioners asked Staff to confirm if bus route 78 along
  Main Street was already taken into consideration within the major
  transit stop map and if it would have any impact upon the map.
  o The Commissioners asked for clarity on whether the Commission
  7
  11/21/2022
   had previously voted to expand the ½ mile major transit district
  area. The Commissioners inquired if this effectively allows for
  unlimited density and no parking requirements in certain areas
  within the City.
  o The Commissioners inquired if the City has improvement plans
  for additional transit options outside of parking. The
  Commissioners expressed the need to understand the
  interconnections with parking and further stated that SCAG’s
  designation of the major transit stops will allow for additional
  consideration of priority improvements to accommodate first and
  last mile efforts.
  Commissioner Comments – Off-Street Parking Standards
  Minimum Requirements for Residential Uses:
  o The Commissioners asked for additional rationale for the
  proposed change to limit off-street single-family residential
  parking to 2 spaces regardless of size. The Commissioners asked
  for further clarification if the off-street parking requirements only
  include garage spaces and not driveway spaces.
  o The Commissioners inquired if there are parking requirements for
  ADUs.
  o The Commissioners asked for clarification that if there were a
  single-family residence proposed within a major transit stop area
  whether a 2-car garage would still be required.
  o The Commissioners asked if the proposed changes would create
  a disincentive to create larger units if greater parking is being
  required, and whether this would be considered a governmental
  constraint.
  o The Commissioners indicated that the increase in parking
  requirements for medium density multiple-family residential does
  seem like a significant change, but stated they were cautious of
  referring to such a change as an impediment to development. The
  Commissioners expressed concern that the number of parking
  spaces required for certain unit sizes does seem a little high, and
  would be supportive of lesser requirements.
  o The Commissioners inquired if the proposed standards for
  medium density residential is intended to off-set lower standards
  for high density residential.
  o The Commissioners expressed support for keeping the standards
  to something that is closer to the current standards, such as
  requiring a ½ parking space per unit.
  o The Commissioners inquired if there is a possibility to allow open
  parking spaces that can be assigned, allowing developments to
  allocate a minimum amount of parking and then designate an area
  of overflow parking that can be allocated as needed to various
  units. The Commissioners further stated it may be helpful to allow
  developments to provide unassigned parking areas and then leave
  it to the property owners/managers to allocate the spaces among

  8
  11/21/2022
   the units.
o  The Commissioners asked Staff if they have a map that illustrates
  the high density areas compared to the transit priority areas.
o  The Commissioners inquired if the high density residential
  standards for parking would be applicable along the Atlantic
  Boulevard corridor, which includes several major transit stops.
  The Commissioners also asked which areas of high density
  residential would be required to comply with the proposed
  parking standard requirements.
o  The Commissioners discussed how there is a lot of residential
  parking spillover onto the streets in existing high density areas
  within the City because there is not enough off-street parking. The
  Commissioners expressed that it would make the streets better if
  future developments were required to provide adequate off-street
  parking for all of their residents.
o  The Commissioners expressed concern that the proposed parking
  requirements would not affect the areas where the existing issues
  are most acute, but indicated support for simplifying the Zoning
  Code.
o  The Commissioners indicated it was helpful to hear the
  perspective of those who live in high density residential areas.
o  The Commissioners stated the proposed new parking
  requirements will not be applicable in many high density
  residential areas, many of which will be exempt from parking
  requirements under State laws, and expressed concern that the
  burden to provide parking will be shifted to smaller developers
  even though the high density residential projects will generate the
  greatest need for parking.
o  The Commissioners inquired if high density residential projects
  that are not required to provide parking will still be allowed to
  obtain overnight parking permits or preferential parking areas for
  its residents. The Commissioners asked if the Commission would
  be able to condition future projects to prohibit the granting of
  overnight parking permits if no off-street parking is being
  provided.
o  The Commissioners stated that even though there may not be
  minimum parking requirements for high density developments,
  that doesn’t necessarily mean developers will not provide any
  parking given the potential challenges with selling units that do
  not have dedicated parking.
o  The Commissioners indicated they may be in favor of increasing
  parking requirements even more so for those properties where
  parking requirements would still be applicable.
o  The Commissioners asked for confirmation that the high density
  residential parking requirements are what would be applicable for
  residential uses in the CBD zone. The Commissioners indicated
  concern with having these parking minimums within the CBD

  9
  11/21/2022
   zone, which is intended to be a walkable area, and inquired if there
  is potential to allow flexibility for projects in the CBD or other
  areas where it makes sense to tailor parking requirements based
  on the unique environment. The Commissioners expressed
  support for minimizing parking requirements in the downtown
  areas to support walkability.
  o The Commissioners asked if the Zoning Code will have different
  parking requirements for affordable housing projects or if this is
  already covered under State law, since affordable housing
  generally requires less parking.
  o The Commissioners inquired as to which density bonus projects
  within the City have utilized a lesser parking standard.
  o The Commissioners asked if there is a minimum threshold for the
  percentage of affordable units under SB 35.
  Commissioner Comments – Off-Street Parking Standards
  Minimum Requirements for Commercial Uses:
  o The Commissioners inquired if the proposed parking
  requirements for automobile sales and leasing includes the
  vehicles on display.
  o The Commissioners asked if the commercial uses category
  includes office spaces or if it only applies to commercial retail
  uses.
  o The Commissioners asked if entertainment uses are defined in the
  Zoning Code.
  o The Commissioners asked for an explanation of the rationale
  behind utilizing area for determining the parking requirements for
  beauty salons. The Commissioners followed-up with an
  additional inquiry if the proposed change will make it more
  consistent with other commercial uses and allow for retail uses to
  more easily convert to beauty salon uses.
  o The Commissioners inquired if outdoor dining areas can be
  exempted from parking requirements. The Commissioners further
  explained that outdoor dining is a great amenity that should be
  supported and the standard requirement for eating and drinking
  establishments works fairly well. The Commissioners support the
  idea of incentivizing outdoor dining by not requiring additional
  parking for these areas. The Commissioners also expressed that in
  the spirit of making things easier when there is a change of use,
  the current parking ratio for eating and drinking establishments
  should be maintained.
  o The Commissioners noted that some jurisdictions have instituted
  a standardized parking requirement in certain areas to enable
  eating and drinking establishments to go into retail tenant spaces
  without having to provide additional parking, which has allowed
  for storefronts to have more activity and less vacancies.
  o The Commissioners suggested instituting different standards for
  outdoor dining and indoor dining parking requirements.

  10
  11/21/2022
   o The Commissioners expressed support for the proposed grocery
  store and medical office parking requirements.
  o The Commissioners inquired if Staff was aware of how existing
  medical offices feel about current parking requirements. The
  Commissioners suggested that Staff outreach to medical office
  businesses to understand their concerns with parking since a
  reduction of parking requirements for these uses may create
  impediments for patients.
  o The Commissioners asked if the same amount of foot traffic is
  being calculated for both grocery stores and medical offices, as
  these two uses may benefit from having different standards.
  o The Commissioners noted that the proposed requirements are the
  parking minimums but that some businesses may want to provide
  more parking based on their own standards.
  Commissioner Comments – Off-Street Parking Standards
  Minimum Requirements for Public/Semi-Public Uses:
  o The Commissioners inquired if the school category also applies to
  tutoring centers.
  o The Commissioners asked what prompted the proposed changes
  in the parking requirements for hospitals and schools.
  o The Commissioners inquired if the proposed new parking
  requirements will only apply to new hospitals and schools, and
  not to existing hospitals and schools.
  Commissioner Comments – Off-Street Parking Standards
  Minimum Requirements for Industrial Uses:
  o The Commissioners asked what the concern was with outdoor
  industrial uses that led to the increase in the parking requirement.
  o The Commissioners asked if mixed-use residential developments
  would be allowed in the industrial zones and if so, how the
  parking standards would be applied at mixed-use projects.
  Commissioner Comments – Off-Street Parking Standards
  General Requirements:
  o The Commissioners inquired if there is a physical design
  difference between long-term and short-term bicycle parking.
  o The Commissioners asked what the rationale was for the number
  of required bicycle parking spaces, and asked Staff if the
  consultant can provide more information on these numbers.
  o The Commissioners stated the number of required bicycle parking
  spaces for residential uses seems a little high and it may need to
  be refined to more realistically reflect what the actual commuting
  patterns may be.
  o The Commissioners suggested requiring 2 bicycle parking spaces
  for every vehicle parking space in a parking structure to encourage
  more bike parking in places that serve office and commercial uses.
  o The Commissioners indicated that the bike parking requirements
  should be flexible to encourage a diverse range of transportation
  options, such as scooters.
  11
  11/21/2022
   o The Commissioners inquired in to how wide the spaces for the
  bicycle parking will be, noting that electric bikes are often larger
  in size than traditional bicycles.
  o The Commissioners expressed support for the proposed changes
  to requirements for parking reductions.
  o The Commissioners requested a study on the utilization of public
  parking facilities. The Commissioners further stated that with
  more mixed-use developments anticipated in the future, there is
  hesitancy with streamlining the parking reduction requirement
  process and having issues arise down the line.
  o The Commissioners inquired if other cities have successfully
  implemented car sharing programs.
  o The Commissioners inquired if Staff considered potential
  programs where employers require employees to pay for parking
  as a method of reducing the number of vehicles parking on site.
  o The Commissioners asked if the car sharing program would
  require designated parking spaces for the car sharing program, and
  if the program includes designated fleet vehicles or if any vehicle
  can be utilized in the program.
  o The Commissioners expressed concern that car sharing programs
  are accessible to anyone and not just residents or tenants of a
  particular site. The Commissioners suggested car sharing
  programs require a Minor Use Permit or some other type of
  entitlement or guidelines to regulate the use before providing a
  reduction of parking.
  o The Commissioners inquired if there are requirements for electric
  vehicle charging stations in the Zoning Code.
    Public Comments:
  Jennifer Ng commented to Staff that she appreciated the
  presentation. Ms. Ng inquired if Staff could provide the PowerPoint
  presentation. Ms. Ng also asked how parking requirements will apply
  to properties on alleyways with no driveway areas.

MOTION:
    Moved to receive and file the informational report.
    Moved by Commissioner Olson, Seconded by Commissioner Wang.
